name: HTTP Security Header Analyzer
problem: Inspect security headers of a site you own and identify missing or weak settings.
objectives: Parse HTTP responses; evaluate header presence and values; produce a report.
arch: CLI -> fetch -> header parser -> rule engine -> JSON/console output
stages: 1. Fetch URL 2. Parse headers 3. Define checks 4. Score each 5. Emit JSON
testing: Run against your own lab server; verify each finding manually.
security: Only scan owned hosts; no aggressive requests.
outcome: A reusable CLI that reports header posture.
github: README with sample output; include checks table; license and authorized-use note.

name: DNS Reconnaissance Utility
problem: Query multiple DNS record types for a domain you own.
objectives: Use dnspython; query A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/NS; present structured results.
arch: CLI -> resolver -> record formatter -> table
stages: 1. Accept domain 2. Query types 3. Handle timeouts 4. Format output
testing: Compare with `dig` output for your domain.
security: Only owned/authorized domains; respect resolver rate limits.
outcome: A DNS lookup tool with clean output.
github: Document record types explained; show example queries.

name: Local Network Analyzer
problem: Inventory devices and open ports on your isolated lab network.
objectives: Use ARP discovery and port scanning safely on a lab segment.
arch: Discover hosts -> probe ports -> store inventory
stages: 1. Discover hosts 2. Probe common ports 3. Store results 4. Report
testing: Run only on host-only lab network; verify with Nmap.
security: Never scan networks you do not own; low rate.
github: Include a network diagram of your lab.

name: Authentication Security Tester
problem: Assess basic authentication controls on a lab app.
objectives: Test session rotation, cookie flags, and rate limiting with your own accounts.
arch: Test harness -> request sequences -> assertions -> report
stages: 1. Capture login 2. Check session rotation 3. Check cookie flags 4. Test rate limits
testing: Run against DVWA/Juice Shop; document each check.
security: Own accounts only; no brute force against real systems.
github: Explain each check and its rationale in README.

name: JWT Security Analyzer
problem: Decode andevaluate JWTs from your own lab; identify common misconfigurations.
objectives: Parse JWT; inspect alg, exp, iss, aud; flag weak settings.
arch: CLI -> decode -> claim checks -> findings
stages: 1. Accept token 2. Decode 3. Check claims 4. Report 5. Note verification limits
testing: Use a token from your own lab app.
security: Never paste production tokens into online tools.

name: API Security Testing Framework
problem: Organize systematic API tests against a lab API.
objectives: Build a request runner with auth, parameter fuzzing, and result logging.
arch: Config -> request templates -> fuzz module -> logger
stages: 1. Load endpoints 2. Add auth 3. Fuzz params 4. Log results 5. Summarize
testing: Test crAPI; verify findings manually.
security: Rate-limit; authorized lab only.
github: Include sample config and redacted results.

name: Subdomain Inventory Tool (Authorized)
problem: Consolidate subdomain data for domains you own into one inventory.
objectives: Merge sources, resolve, deduplicate, and mark liveness.
arch: Sources -> merge -> resolve -> HTTP probe -> CSV
stages: 1. Load seed list 2. Merge sources 3. Resolve 4. Probe gently 5. Export
testing: Compare with manual `httpx` results for your domain.
security: Only owned domains; passive-first; low rate.
github: Show data-flow diagram and output schema.

name: Web Technology Fingerprinting Tool
problem: Identify technologies used by sites you own from observable signals.
objectives: Parse headers, cookies, HTML, and JS names to infer stack.
arch: Fetch -> feature extractor -> signature matcher -> report
stages: 1. Fetch 2. Extract signals 3. Match rules 4. Report with confidence
testing: Validate against browser DevTools for your site.
security: Own sites only; treat results as hints.
outcome: A fingerprinting report with confidence levels.
github: Include rule file format and examples.

name: Security Misconfiguration Scanner (Local Lab)
problem: Detect common misconfigurations in your own lab apps.
objectives: Check headers, directory listings, default pages, and debug endpoints.
arch: Checks -> request engine -> findings -> report
stages: 1. Define checks 2. Run on lab 3. Verify manually 4. Report
testing: Run against DVWA/Juice Shop; confirm each finding.
security: Lab only; no scanning third parties.

name: Automated Report Generator
problem: Produce draft vulnerability reports from structured findings data.
objectives: Template engine for consistent report output.
arch: Findings JSON -> template -> Markdown/PDF
stages: 1. Define schema 2. Build template 3. Render 4. Review
testing: Generate a sample report from a lab finding.
security: No real data; review before submission.

name: Browser Security Analysis Tool
problem: Analyze client-side security signals in your own site.
objectives: Inspect CSP, cookie flags, SOP/CORS headers, and storage usage.
arch: Fetch -> analyze headers/HTML -> report
stages: 1. Collect headers 2. Analyze CSP 3. Check cookies 4. Report
testing: Cross-check with DevTools on your site.
security: Own site only.

name: JavaScript Endpoint Analyzer
problem: Extract API endpoints from JS bundles of apps you own.
objectives: Download bundles; regex/parse for paths and methods; deduplicate.
arch: Crawl -> bundle fetch -> extractor -> endpoint list
stages: 1. Find script tags 2. Fetch bundles 3. Extract paths 4. Dedup 5. Report
testing: Compare with Katana output on your app.
security: Own apps only; avoid secret leakage.

name: Secure File Upload Testing Lab
problem: Build a lab that demonstrates upload validation failures and fixes.
objectives: Create an app with and without safe upload handling; compare.
arch: Flask app -> upload handler -> validation -> storage
stages: 1. Build vulnerable version 2. Test bypasses 3. Implement allowlist 4. Retest
testing: Upload harmless marker files only.
security: Isolated lab; never expose publicly.
outcome: A teaching lab with before/after code.
github: Include a write-up of bypass classes.

name: SQL Injection Demonstration Lab
problem: Build a lab app showing injection and parameterized-query fixes.
objectives: Compare concatenated vs. parameterized queries.
arch: App -> query layer -> toggle vulnerable/safe -> UI
stages: 1. Build search form 2. Add vuln query 3. Demonstrate 4. Fix 5. Verify
testing: Use only local test data.
security: Lab only; no real data.

name: XSS Demonstration Lab
problem: Demonstrate reflected, stored, and DOM XSS with harmless payloads.
objectives: Build pages with and without encoding; show context differences.
arch: Flask app -> templates -> payload handling -> CSP toggle
stages: 1. Reflected case 2. Stored case 3. DOM sink 4. Add encoding/CSP 5. Verify
testing: Use marker strings, not real cookies.
security: Lab only; no third-party testing.

name: SSRF Prevention and Validation Lab
problem: Build a URL-fetch feature and demonstrate SSRF plus defenses.
objectives: Show allow-listing and private-range blocking.
arch: Fetch endpoint -> validator -> egress -> log
stages: 1. Vulnerable fetch 2. Demonstrate local fetch 3. Add allowlist 4. Verify
testing: Use a local listener as target.
security: Lab only; no cloud metadata.
github: Diagram the request flow and defenses.

name: OAuth Security Laboratory
problem: Simulate an OAuth flow and demonstrate state/PKCE failures.
objectives: Implement authorization code + PKCE; show attacks when omitted.
arch: Mock IdP -> client -> token endpoint -> tests
stages: 1. Build flow 2. Add state/PKCE 3. Demo CSRF without state 4. Fix
testing: Use local mock provider only.
security: No real providers; no real credentials.
outcome: An OAuth flow demo with attack/fix toggles.

name: GraphQL Authorization Testing Lab
problem: Build a GraphQL API with resolver-level authorization gaps.
objectives: Test BOLA and depth abuse; add complexity limits.
arch: GraphQL server -> resolvers -> auth layer -> tests
stages: 1. Build schema 2. Two tenants 3. Test cross-tenant 4. Add auth 5. Add depth limits
testing: Use two test tenants.
security: Lab only.
github: Document queries that failed and why.

name: Race Condition Demonstration Lab
problem: Build a coupon-redemption endpoint with a TOCTOU flaw and fix it.
objectives: Demonstrate parallel requests and atomic remediation.
arch: Endpoint -> check/use -> DB -> lock
stages: 1. Build flawed flow 2. Parallel test 3. Add transaction/lock 4. Retest
testing: Use your own test account and coupon.
security: Lab only; avoid load on shared systems.

name: Docker Security Analyzer
problem: Audit your own Docker images and containers for misconfigurations.
objectives: Check root user, privileged mode, exposed ports, and image CVEs.
arch: Docker API/inspect -> rule engine -> report
stages: 1. List containers 2. Inspect configs 3. Scan images 4. Report
testing: Scan only your lab images.
security: Own images only; do not scan shared registries.
github: Map findings to CIS Docker Benchmark.

name: Cloud IAM Configuration Analyzer
problem: Analyze IAM policies in your own lab cloud account.
objectives: Parse policies for wildcards and over-privilege.
arch: Export policies -> parser -> risk rules -> report
stages: 1. Export IAM 2. Parse 3. Flag wildcards 4. Report
testing: Use a free-tier lab account only.
security: Own account; read-only calls.

name: Dependency Vulnerability Analyzer
problem: Scan a lab project for vulnerable dependencies and triage results.
objectives: Use Trivy/Grype; map findings to reachability.
arch: Project -> SBOM -> scanner -> triage table
stages: 1. Generate SBOM 2. Scan 3. Triage 4. Prioritize fixes
testing: Scan your own project.
security: No data exfiltration; official DBs.

name: Secret Scanning Tool
problem: Scan your own repositories for accidentally committed secrets.
objectives: Use regex/entropy rules; scan git history.
arch: Repo -> history scan -> detectors -> report
stages: 1. Scan working tree 2. Scan history 3. Triage 4. Rotate test secrets
testing: Create a repo with a fake key pattern.
security: Never commit real secrets; rotate if found.

name: Android Application Security Analyzer
problem: Perform static analysis on a lab APK.
objectives: Use MobSF/JADX to identify manifest and code issues.
arch: APK -> decode -> decompile -> findings
stages: 1. Decode manifest 2. Decompile 3. Review storage/crypto 4. Report
testing: Use a deliberately vulnerable APK.
security: Own apps only; no distribution.
github: Explain each finding with code references.

name: Fuzzing Harness
problem: Build a fuzzing harness for a small parser you own.
objectives: Create harness, run AFL++/libFuzzer, triage crashes.
arch: Harness -> fuzzer -> corpus -> crash triage
stages: 1. Write parser 2. Harness 3. Fuzz 4. Minimize 5. Root-cause
testing: Fuzz only your own code.
security: Isolated lab; no network targets.

name: Binary Crash Analysis Tool
problem: Automate triage of crashes from a lab fuzzing run.
objectives: Group crashes by stack signature; use GDB/ASan reports.
arch: Crash corpus -> debugger -> signature -> report
stages: 1. Collect crashes 2. Deduplicate 3. Analyze 4. Report
testing: Use crashes from your own fuzzer.
security: Lab only; no untrusted binaries.

name: RAG Security Testing Framework
problem: Test tenant isolation and retrieval poisoning in a lab RAG app.
objectives: Seed markers; attempt cross-tenant retrieval and prompt injection.
arch: Two tenants -> vector store -> retriever -> assertions
stages: 1. Seed markers 2. Query cross-tenant 3. Poison doc 4. Add filters 5. Retest
testing: Use only seeded markers.
security: Own lab app; no third-party models with secrets.

name: LLM Prompt Injection Evaluation Framework
problem: Evaluate prompt injection resistance of a local model/app.
objectives: Build a test suite of harmless injection cases and score outcomes.
arch: Case list -> runner -> classifier -> scoring
stages: 1. Define cases 2. Run 3. Classify 4. Score 5. Report
testing: Use a local model endpoint.
security: No real user data; label safety vs security.

name: AI Agent Tool-Permission Auditor
problem: Audit tool scopes and authorization in a lab agent.
objectives: Enumerate tools, check scopes, test unauthorized calls.
arch: Agent config -> tool inventory -> permission tests -> report
stages: 1. List tools 2. Review scopes 3. Test low-priv calls 4. Add policy gate 5. Verify
testing: Use only mock tools in your lab.
security: No real actions or data.

name: Personal Bug Bounty Research Dashboard
problem: Build a dashboard tracking programs, findings, and learning.
objectives: Aggregate your journals and reports into usable metrics.
arch: Data model -> importer -> dashboard -> charts
stages: 1. Define schema 2. Import logs 3. Build views 4. Charts 5. Review
testing: Use your own synthetic data.
security: Keep reports confidential; no program secrets.
